preamble: Deaffrication of the alveolar affricate [ts] to the plain stop [t], losing the fricative release. The best-known case is the merger of Proto-Austronesian *C with *t in Proto-Malayo-Polynesian, the ancestor of all Austronesian languages outside Taiwan. Blust reconstructs *C as a voiceless alveolar affricate, so words such as *maCa 'eye', *Caliŋa 'ear' and *Cau 'person' appear with t across Malayo-Polynesian (Malay mata, Tagalog matá, Fijian daliŋa), while several Formosan languages keep an affricate or sibilant (Paiwan matsa, Thao maca). Within Taiwan, Amis also shows t for *C. Some scholars (Ross, Shibata) reconstruct *C as retroflex rather than alveolar, so the exact starting sound is debated.

examples.to: PMP *mata (Tagalog matá, Indonesian mata, Javanese mata, Samoan matā)
examples.note: Compare Formosan Paiwan matsa, Thao maca, Proto-Rukai maca, which keep the affricate or sibilant.

examples.to: PMP *taliŋa (Tagalog taʔíŋa, Malay teliŋa, Fijian daliŋa)

examples.note: Amis shows t for *C, unlike Paiwan matsa and Thao maca.
Wolaytta has geminate /tt/ where neighbouring Ometo varieties have /ts/, in mitta, hatta, haytta, suutta 'blood' and mek'etta 'bone' (Blažek 2008 word list).
